name: Olive oil
best_for: sauteing, roasting, dressings; refined olive oil for frying
traditional_in: Mediterranean: Spain, Italy, Greece, Turkey, the Levant, North Africa

name: Canola / rapeseed oil
traditional_in: Canada and the US (canola); Northern Europe, China and India (rapeseed)

name: Vegetable oil (blend)
notes: In the US usually soybean oil or a soybean / canola / corn blend; check the label

name: Soybean oil
notes: Highly refined soybean oil is exempt from US allergen labeling (FALCPA)

name: Sunflower oil
notes: High-oleic sunflower oil is more stable for frying

name: Peanut (groundnut) oil
traditional_in: China, West Africa, Southeast Asia, US Southern frying
notes: Highly refined peanut oil is exempt from US allergen labeling; cold-pressed, expeller-pressed or extruded peanut oil is not. Always warn.

name: Sesame oil
best_for: flavoring and finishing (toasted); light sesame oil for frying
traditional_in: China, Korea, Japan, South India (gingelly oil), the Middle East
notes: Toasted sesame oil is mostly used as a seasoning rather than a frying fat

name: Coconut oil
traditional_in: South India (Kerala), Sri Lanka, Southeast Asia, the Caribbean, the Pacific
notes: FDA no longer lists coconut as a tree nut (2025 guidance); some people are still allergic to it

name: Palm oil (red palm / dende)
traditional_in: West and Central Africa (Nigeria, Ghana, Cameroon), Brazil (Bahia), Southeast Asia

name: Mustard oil
traditional_in: Bengal and Eastern India, Bangladesh, Nepal, Punjab
notes: Mustard is a labeled allergen in the EU and Canada (not one of the US major allergens)

name: Cottonseed oil
traditional_in: US South, Egypt, the Middle East

name: Walnut oil
notes: No value in the smoke point source; usually not heated

name: Hazelnut oil
notes: No value in the smoke point source; usually not heated

name: Butter
traditional_in: France and Northern Europe, US baking
notes: Burns at high heat; clarify it (ghee) for frying

name: Ghee / clarified butter
traditional_in: India, Pakistan, Bangladesh; smen (North Africa); niter kibbeh (Ethiopia, spiced)
notes: Spiced versions (niter kibbeh) are mapped to ghee. USDA value is for anhydrous butter oil (the same fat as ghee): the SR Legacy ghee entry has no monounsaturated value

name: Margarine
notes: Some margarines contain whey or other milk ingredients; check the label

name: Vegetable shortening
animal_source: possible (some blends contain lard or tallow)
notes: Usually soybean or palm; some shortenings are lard or tallow blends

name: Lard
traditional_in: Mexico, Central Europe, China, US South

name: Chicken fat (schmaltz)
traditional_in: Ashkenazi Jewish cooking, Central and Eastern Europe

name: Duck or goose fat
notes: USDA value is for goose fat

name: Cooking spray
notes: Usually canola or soybean oil; some contain milk or soy lecithin

name: Oil (type not stated)
notes: The recipe says only 'oil' or 'oil for frying': the fat could be peanut, sesame or animal fat, so allergy and diet checks must warn
